caption: Samaltak · Live. Everything in this video changes a running system, driven through samaltak-ctl.
spoken: [warm] Okay, this one's fun. Everything you're about to see changes a running system. No restarts, no tricks.

caption: The theme is a Smalltalk class: change the accent in the System Browser, ⌘S, and every window restyles at once.
spoken: Let's start with the look. The theme is just a class. Change the accent colour, save, and [pause] every window picks it up, while the Mandelbrot keeps rendering.

caption: The GPU shader is Smalltalk source too: edit the Renderer's MSL, ⌘S, and the pipeline is rebuilt.
spoken: Even the GPU shader is a Smalltalk method. Edit it, save, and the whole screen changes. [pause] Okay, let's put that back.

caption: Glyphs are rasterized in Smalltalk from the .ttf on disk: change the coverage and every text re-rasterizes.
spoken: The fonts are rasterized in Smalltalk, straight from the TrueType file. Make the coverage a little heavier, and all the text gets bolder. These are the actual pixels.

caption: One setting slows the animation clock tenfold: window open, menu, selection glide, the debugger's pc highlight.
spoken: Now let's slow time down. Ten times slower, so you can see every little animation. [pause] And back to normal speed.

caption: Edit and continue mid-computation: change the Mandelbrot's colouring while it renders; the rows still to come use it.
spoken: Here's the Mandelbrot, halfway through a render. Change its colour function, save, and [pause] the rows it hasn't drawn yet come out in the new colours.

caption: [true] whileTrue: that Process is busy, everything else stays smooth. ⌘. opens a debugger inside the loop.
spoken: Act two: you can't break it. An infinite loop. That process is stuck, but everything else stays smooth. Command-period, and we're in a debugger, right inside the loop.

caption: Break in the Transcript's own Process (Window>>redraw): it freezes in a debugger, every other window keeps working.
spoken: Let's stop the window system itself. A breakpoint in redraw, only for the Transcript's process. It freezes, everything else keeps going. Write to it from the debugger, remove the breakpoint, proceed, [pause] and it catches up.

caption: Debugging the debugger: a breakpoint in its own Step Over, and a second debugger opens on the first.
spoken: Can we debug the debugger? Sure. A breakpoint in its own step over, step, [pause] and a second debugger opens on the first one.

caption: Halt on write on a window's bounds: drag it, and the debugger shows the window-manager code that moved it.
spoken: Watch a window's bounds, then drag it. We land right in the window manager code that moved it, and the mouse still works.

caption: Infinite recursion: a debugger on the stack, not a crash.
spoken: And infinite recursion? [pause] Just a debugger. No crash.

caption: Save the image with a debugger stopped mid-step, quit, relaunch: every window is back, the process still suspended. Step on.
spoken: Act three. Save the image with a debugger open, mid-step, and quit. [pause] Relaunch, and everything's back, the process still waiting where we left it. Step, and it just continues.

caption: The core is small: in the Terminal (Smalltalk too) count C and Smalltalk lines, then race GNU Smalltalk on the same benchmarks.
spoken: Last thing. How much of this is C? Let's ask a terminal, which, yes, is Smalltalk too. Count the lines, [pause] and race the same benchmarks against GNU Smalltalk.

caption: All of it live, in one running image, driven through samaltak-ctl.
spoken: [warm] All of that, live, in one running image. Thanks for watching!
